Use per-user paired outcomes: d(c,u)=hit_A(c,u)−hit_B(c,u), with hits defined by the unchanged evaluator and identical candidate pools. The macro difference is Δ=(1/4)Σc mean_u d(c,u). Adapting [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/), independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, keeping both models’ outcomes paired; recompute Δ over, for example, 10,000 replicates and report its 2.5th–97.5th percentiles. Retain equal category weights; do not resample the four categories when inference concerns these four fixed datasets. Report category differences and discordant counts: A-only hits versus B-only hits. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points; this resolution is not a significance threshold.

These intervals estimate user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted models, training seed 42, splits and fixed candidate pools, assuming users are independent within categories. They do not measure training-seed variability or robustness to alternative negative samples. Identical pools support paired comparisons but do not remove sampled-evaluation bias: sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings. Interpret results specifically as pinned 100-candidate HR@10; preserve the evaluator without corrections. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Repeatedly choosing architectures, epochs or hyperparameters on these same users creates selection optimism; an ordinary bootstrap interval around the selected winner does not correct it. Treat small validation gains as exploratory, report search breadth, and avoid calling an interval crossing zero evidence of equivalence. For prespecified multiple comparisons, use multiplicity control such as Holm; it does not resolve unrestricted adaptive search. Freeze the selected model before the host’s final held-out evaluation. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html).
